con-fulgĕo , ēre,
I.v. n., to shine brightly, to glitter, glisten (very rare; “perh. only in the foll. exs.): aedes confulgebant,” Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 15 ; 5, 1, 44: lucida confulgent alti carchesia mali, Cinna ap. Isid. Orig. 19, 2, 10.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
